about: V0 roadside things for the world knowledge graph. Hand-written, reviewed. Learned numbers go to priors CSV files made by learn_roadside.py; this file holds the thing definitions, the OSM match rules, the completeness gates, and the written-standard rules. Every value has a 'why' or a source id from sources.json. Values marked confidence 'low' are expert starting values that a learned or audited value must replace.

contexts.about: Context fields for V0. The first four are made by learn_roadside.py from the OSM download alone. The others are hooks that the scan engine fills at run time; the learning script adds them when the PC has the rasters.

fields.from: OSM highway tag (links join their parent class; living_street joins residential)
road km per km2 in the 1 km cell, drivable roads without driveways and parking aisles
fields.why: road density is complete in US OSM (TIGER base) and tracks building density; housing-unit density from the Census replaces it when the PC has the ACS block groups

fields.from: side of the way in OSM drawing direction; used only for offsets and fences
NLCD class of the roadside cell (scan engine CLAS)
Census tract median year built (NSI med_yr_blt or ACS B25035)
3DEP terrain slope at the road edge

things.name: Fire hydrant

completeness.why: towns with water mains have hydrants on almost every block; a well-mapped county has them in nearly every dense cell

attach.why: behind the kerb or at the back of the verge; learned offset distribution replaces this

excludes.why: hydrants are not set in a driveway mouth

things.variant_rule: wet barrel in frost-free climates (Koppen A, BWh, Csa coastal), dry barrel elsewhere; confidence low
things.colour_rule: body colour is chosen per water utility (one colour per city block group, often yellow, red, silver or chrome yellow); bonnet and caps by flow class: light blue >= 1500 gpm, green 1000-1499, orange 500-999, red < 500
things.collision_note: traffic-model hydrants break at a flange; the car team sets mass and break force

things.name: Utility pole (power or telecom)

completeness.why: overhead lines run along most rural and suburban roads but not all; a lower gate because true gaps exist (buried lines)

size_m.why: common US distribution poles are 35-45 ft long with about 10 % plus 2 ft set in the ground

attach.why: learned offset replaces this; often at the right-of-way line

spacing_check.why: distribution spans; the learned gap distribution is the value used

co_occurs.learn: share of street lights within 2 m of a pole, per county

things.variant_rule: wood in most places; concrete or steel more common in hurricane coasts and new urban lines; learn from OSM material tag where present
things.real_3d: mesh; wires are real 3D catenary splines between poles (sag 1-3 % of span)

things.name: Street light
things.variant_rule: acorn post-top only in mapped historic districts and town centres; high mast only at motorway interchanges; others learned (share on utility poles)
things.night: lit; lamp type by era and region (LED 3000-4000 K after about 2015 conversions, high-pressure sodium before); the picture thread owns light units

things.name: Residential curbside mailbox
things.why_rule: residential mailboxes are almost never in OSM; their count follows houses and the USPS delivery mode

rule.count: one per house served by a curbside delivery; two to six on one shared post where houses share a driveway or a rural route turn-out

delivery_mode_prior.why: USPS requires centralized delivery for most new delivery points since about 2012

rule.confidence: low; replace with a Mapillary or street-photo audit (v2.0.4)

placement.why: USPS curbside mailbox guidance: box bottom 41-45 in above the road, front 6-8 in back from the kerb or road edge

rule.side_rule: on the driveway side next to the road; on busy rural routes the boxes can be grouped on the carrier's right side (confidence low)

things.variant_rule: brick or stone column more common in the South and in 1990+ suburbs; novelty boxes rare (about 1 %); block lumpiness high (neighbours copy)

things.name: Delineator post (reflector post)
things.why_rule: delineators are almost never in OSM; MUTCD gives the spacing

rule.where: rural motorway and trunk always; rural primary and secondary where the state uses them (learned share per state later); at curves, bridge ends, and lane drops
rule.curve_spacing: S = 3 * sqrt(R - 50), S and R in feet, S between 20 and 300 ft; the spacing ahead of and after the curve is 2S, then 3S, then 6S
rule.lateral_why: 2 to 8 ft outside the outer edge of the shoulder
rule.colour: white on the right, yellow on the left of one-way roadways and median
rule.confidence: medium (values from the MUTCD 2009 Chapter 3F; confirm in the 11th edition, 2023)

things.name: Fence along the road
things.measure: share of road length (each side) with a fence or hedge within 3-40 m that runs within 30 degrees of the road direction

completeness.why: rural fences are mapped much less than city things; a county passes when fences appear along most rural road cells; the rest is from rules and the audit

variant_prior.why: crop fields are often not fenced

things.block_lumpiness: very high: one owner fences a whole parcel edge with one type
things.real_3d: posts and rails real 3D; wire and mesh as alpha cards near, a line far

things.name: Guard rail (W-beam)
things.measure: share of road length per class with a guard rail within 6 m
things.rule_fallback: at bridge ends (with a flared or buried end terminal), on fills higher than about 3 m with steep side slopes, and on the outside of sharp curves on mountain roads; confidence medium; geometry from the CORR cross-section and lidar
things.real_3d: real 3D; the car can hit it (collision rigid with energy absorption, car team)

things.name: Culvert end (pipe under the road or a driveway)
things.measure: share of mapped stream crossings that are culverts, by road class; culvert ends are placed where the stream meets the fill toe on both sides

rule.driveway_culvert: a rural driveway that crosses a roadside ditch gets a pipe: p 0.85 in humid climates (Koppen C, D), 0.4 in dry climates (B) where dips are common; pipe 0.3-0.45 m corrugated metal, sometimes concrete, with or without a mitred end
rule.confidence: low; check with the street-photo audit

things.variant_rule: pipe size and end by road class and stream order (NHD); box culverts for bigger streams under primary roads
things.real_3d: real 3D end and opening (the driver sees the dark hole); the pipe is short

things.name: Stop sign (R1-1)
things.measure: P(stop | approach class, crossing class) per junction; all-way stop share at equal classes

rule.imagine_only_if: the learned P >= 0.9 for the minor approach of a mapped junction with a higher class road; the traffic code reads the same record (gotcha 8.16)
rule.source_why: MUTCD 2009 Sections 2A.18-2A.19 and 2B.01; confirm in the 11th edition

things.name: Speed limit sign (R2-1)
things.why_rule: speed signs are rarely mapped as nodes; the maxspeed tag on ways is common

place_at: each maxspeed change, facing the new limit, both directions
30-150 m after a junction with a road of class tertiary or higher
rural repeat every 3-8 km (confidence low; state practice differs)
rule.confidence: medium for change points, low for repeats; learn from Mapillary traffic-sign map features in v2.0.4

things.name: Curve warning sign (W1 series) and chevrons

rule.advisory_speed: from the curve radius and superelevation in the CORR cross-section: V^2 = 15 R (e + f), V mph, R ft, f side friction by speed (AASHTO), rounded down to 5 mph; or the ball-bank method (16 deg below 20 mph, 14 deg at 25-30 mph, 12 deg at 35 mph and up)
rule.when: speed difference = posted (maxspeed) minus advisory: 5 mph recommend the sign; 10 mph require the sign and the advisory speed plaque, recommend chevrons; 15 mph or more require chevrons (MUTCD 2009 Table 2C-5, for arterials and collectors with AADT >= 1000; on other roads use as an option with p 0.6)
rule.sign_type: W1-1 curve if advisory >= 35 mph, W1-2 turn if below 30 mph; W1-5 or W1-4 for reverse curves closer than 600 ft; W1-8 chevrons on the outside of the curve, spaced so 2-3 are seen at once
rule.place: before the curve, distance from MUTCD Table 2C-4 by speed (about 30-200 m)
rule.confidence: medium; this also gives the driver real advisory speeds on the Dragon

co_occurs.learn: P(bench within 15 m | bus stop) from bench=yes tags and bench nodes

things.name: Public trash bin
things.dyn_note: residential carts at the kerb on collection day are a later DYN thing (gotcha 8.13)

rule_count_note: 14 entries: the 12 V0 things plus guard rail (split from fence) and the blue collection box (it is the OSM post_box, often confused with home mailboxes). 9 are learned from OSM, 5 come from written standards (mailbox, delineator, speed sign, curve sign, driveway culvert).
